### **4.3 Generalization and Boundaries of the One-Action Rule (§6.6 Q18)**

The reduction of the Dashboard from eleven blocks to three (U5) was driven by the principle *"one screen, one action"*1. Answering **§6.6 Q18** (*"Does that rule generalise to every screen in the rebuild?"*): **The rule generalizes strictly to every Diagnostic, Summary, Gate, and Transition screen, where there must be exactly one primary \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue button on the screen; however, it does NOT generalize to force multi-control Sitting Workspaces and Unlocked Catalogues into a single button, where instead it operates as a strict "One Primary Action Hierarchy" rule (at most one \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue button on screen, paired with secondary \#ffffff ink-framed controls)**1.

| Screen Category | Screens Governed | How the One-Action Rule Applies (§6.6 Q18) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Category 1: Strict Single-Action Decision Surfaces** | SCR-DB-01 (Dashboard), SCR-PL-01 (Placement Preflight), SCR-PL-04 (Placement Results), SCR-LP-03 (Terminal Readiness Verdict), SCR-EX-03 (Mock Exam Results). | **Strict 1-Action Enforcement**: The screen answers a diagnostic question and funnels the learner into **one deterministic primary \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue CTA** (e.g., BẮT ĐẦU BƯỚC 5 NGAY on Dashboard; XEM LỘ TRÌNH HỌC 4 TUẦN on Placement Results)1. Any secondary utility (such as retrying an unmeasured skill U11 or viewing an archive) is rendered as a secondary \#ffffff ink-framed control inside its specific row, never as a competing top-level \#0b4ea2 button1. |
| **Category 2: Guided Timeline & Catalogue Surfaces** | SCR-LP-01 (Learning Path Timeline), SCR-PRAC-01..03 (Practice Hubs when Free Drilling is unlocked), SCR-EX-01 (Mock Exam Catalogue). | **Single Primary Highlight \+ Secondary Catalogue Controls**: Even when multiple steps or unlocked free-drill topics are visible on screen, **only the single next scheduled step in ![][image46] (or the \#1 Recommended Free Drill when ![][image46] is done per L2) carries the solid \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue button fill**1. All other selectable topic rows or mock exams use \#ffffff painted buttons with 2px solid \#14181d frames so the eye is guided to one primary starting point while retaining free exploration (L2)1. |
| **Category 3: Active Sitting & Practice Workspaces** | SCR-PL-02/03 (Placement Sittings), SCR-PRAC-04/05 (Practice Sessions), SCR-LS-01 (Lesson View), SCR-EX-02 (Mock Exam Sitting). | **Workspace Exception (Multi-Control by Construct Necessity)**: During an active sitting (FR-SERVE-02, FR-SERVE-03), the candidate must simultaneously read/scroll a passage, select options A–D across child items, flag an item (\#f2b705 Sign Gold), navigate backward/forward within the active stage (FR-SERVE-03), and submit the stage1. Forcing a 200-question exam or a multi-item reading passage into a single-action wizard would violate psychometric local review rules (FR-SERVE-03) and the high-density mandate (§4)1. Here, option selection uses \#14181d ink inversion (§4), navigation uses \#ffffff ink-framed buttons, and **only the terminal stage/task commit button (NỘP BÀI / TIẾP TỤC SANG GIAI ĐOẠN 2\) uses \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue**1. |

### **4.4 Streaming AI Commentary vs. Structured JSON Grading Reveal (U1, U3, U4, U9, U12)**

When a learner submits a Speaking or Writing task on SCR-PRAC-05, the backend pipeline produces two distinct data structures: a **deterministic structured JSON grading record** (criteria\_scores, composite\_mean, verbatim error quotes, and suggested rewrites) and **narrative diagnostic prose (ai\_insight)**1. Decisions U1, U3, U4, U9, and U12 govern their exact client-side presentation1. Because streaming into a half-built JSON object has no meaningful user interface (U1), the structured JSON grading output is never streamed token-by-token; while the four dimension-decoupled LLM rubric calls (2.md §4.3) are executing, the top **Rubric & Error Record Panel** displays a 2px solid \#14181d frame with the monospace status \[ĐANG CHẤM ĐIỂM THEO 4 TIÊU CHÍ RUBRIC...\]1. The instant the JSON payload parses on the client, the panel reveals progressively across three crisp structural blocks (150ms step interval, zero blur or fade): first, the composite score paired with the \[ĐIỂM DO AI ƯỚC TÍNH\] badge (U12); second, the 4-criterion tabular meter (c1..c4); and third, the table of verbatim extracted error spans paired with suggested rewrites1.  
Directly beneath the Rubric Record Panel sits the **Diagnostic Commentary Signboard (NHẬN XÉT CHI TIẾT TỪ HỆ THỐNG CHẤM AI)** framed in 2px solid \#14181d on a flat \#ffffff field with zero chat bubbles, zero AI avatars, and zero gradients (U3)1. As narrative prose tokens arrive over the Server-Sent Events stream (U1), text renders in font-reading (\#14181d) trailed immediately by a **solid \#14181d ink block cursor (width: 8px; height: 16px; display: inline-block, blinking via a hard steps(1) 500ms CSS keyframe with zero opacity fade per U3)**1. When the stream finishes (\[DONE\]), Decision U9 mandates that the block cursor disappears immediately and a 1px solid \#ccd2d6 footer rule appears at the bottom of the panel recording the exact generation timestamp in monospace ("Nhận xét được tạo lúc 14:22:09 ngày 04/11/2026 (cho lần nộp bài \#02)") so a learner who practices again never mistakes an older insight for a new one1. If the stream breaks mid-sentence due to a network drop or timeout, Decision U4 mandates that the interface **never clears or discards the text already shown on screen**: the cursor stops, the partial text remains fixed in place, and a 2px solid \#f2b705 Sign Gold bar appends directly below the last rendered word (\[NHẬN XÉT CHƯA HOÀN CHỈNH DO NGẮT KẾT NỐI MẠNG — NỘI DUNG ĐÃ HIỂN THỊ ĐƯỢC GIỮ NGUYÊN\]) beside a \#0b4ea2 Sign Blue button TẢI LẠI PHẦN NHẬN XÉT CÒN THIẾU1.

### **4.5 Audit of External Design-Reference Patterns Accepted vs. Refused (§7.1)**

In accordance with Section 7.1 of the brief, standard assessment and EdTech UI pattern libraries were evaluated during the preparation of this specification, taking their structural and ergonomic reasoning while refusing their visual styling where it conflicted with **"Bảng hiệu phòng thi"**1.

| Pattern Domain | External Design-System Generator / Pattern Proposal | Refused Properties (Forbidden by §4 & §7.1) | Adopted Structural & Ergonomic Principles (Applied in This SRS) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Assessment Dashboard & Skill Cards** | Modern EdTech SaaS / Claymorphism (16–24px rounded cards, soft double drop shadows, indigo/violet gradient hero banner, radial circular progress gauges). | **Refused**: All rounded corners (border-radius \> 0), all box-shadow elevations, all indigo/pastel palettes, all gradient hero backgrounds, and circular donut gauges1. | **Adopted**: Strict visual hierarchy separating the primary next action (Block 1\) from reference telemetry (Blocks 2 & 3), alignment of DOM tab order with left-to-right visual reading order, and high-contrast AAA-level foreground/background pairing (\#14181d on \#ffffff)1. |
| **AI Grading & Feedback Interface** | Conversational AI Assistant UI (rounded chat bubbles, robot/sparkle avatar icons, animated shimmer skeletons, token streaming of raw JSON or markdown cards). | **Refused**: Chat bubbles, AI avatars/sparkle icons, gradient text shimmers, and streaming into half-built score cards (U1, U3)1. | **Adopted**: Streaming long-form diagnostic prose (U1) with a terminal block cursor (U3) instead of blocking on a full-section spinner; preserving already-read text on stream failure (U4); atomic rendering of structured rubric tables1. |
| **Multidimensional Score Reporting** | Psychometric Score Report Guidelines (Hambleton & Zenisky, 2013; Wainer et al., 1999): Aligned horizontal scale strips with explicit benchmark lines and error/status qualifiers. | **Refused**: Multi-axis radar/spider charts (which distort area perception when 1 of 4 skills is low and collapse into a flat line on 2-skill certificates) and colour-only red/green delta badges1. | **Adopted**: Aligned horizontal scale strips (Pre-A1..C2) sharing a common vertical target line across all skill rows (SCR-PL-04), explicit verbal \+ numeric pairing for every delta, and distinct visual encoding for unmeasured (U11) vs. low-proficiency states1. |

## **5\. Content, Copy, and Data-Formatting Rules**

The platform has previously shipped defects where raw database enum keys (such as below\_A1) reached the learner's eyes and where a numerical drop caused by crossing a band boundary was painted in error red or a score drop painted in success green1. The copy and formatting rules below are mandatory across every component1.

### **5.1 Database Key Translation and Enum Sanitization Gate**

Under **Rule COPY-01 (Strict Enum Sanitization Gate)**, no database enum value, table code, or internal identifier from PlacementTests, PlacementSkillResults, LearningPaths, PathSteps, or CertificateBands may ever be interpolated directly into a DOM text node1. Every backend enum must pass through a compile-time TypeScript lookup dictionary (DisplayLabelRegistry) with an exhaustive switch check; if an unmapped key is encountered at runtime, the UI logs a telemetry error and renders a safe fallback ("Bậc năng lực đang cập nhật"), never a raw string containing underscores (\_)1.

| Raw Database Key / Internal Code (2.md & 3.md) | Forbidden Raw Printout | Mandatory Learner-Facing Display String (font-signage / font-mono) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| below\_A1 / Pre-A1 | below\_A1 | DƯỚI A1 (MỨC KHỞI ĐẦU) |
| CAT\_B1, CAT\_B2, SW\_B1, SW\_B2 | CAT\_B1, SW\_B2 | B1 (TOEIC ADAPTIVE), B2 (TOEIC ADAPTIVE), B1 (TOEIC NÓI & VIẾT), B2 (TOEIC NÓI & VIẾT) |
| TOEIC\_LR, TOEIC\_CAT, TOEIC\_SW | TOEIC\_LR, TOEIC\_CAT | TOEIC Nghe & Đọc (4 Kỹ năng), TOEIC Adaptive (Nghe & Đọc), TOEIC Nói & Viết |
| short\_maintenance, standard, expanded\_remedial | expanded\_remedial | BƯỚC DUY TRÌ (5 CÂU), BƯỚC TIÊU CHUẨN, BƯỚC CỦNG CỐ CHUYÊN SÂU |
| feasible, stretch, unrealistic, cannot\_judge | cannot\_judge, stretch | KHẢ THI, CẦN CỐ GẮNG (SÁT NÚT), QUÁ TẢI (CẦN ĐIỀU CHỈNH), CHƯA ĐỦ DỮ LIỆU ĐÁNH GIÁ GIỜ HỌC |
| reused\_from\_prior, not\_measured, grading | not\_measured | SỬ DỤNG LẠI KẾT QUẢ CŨ, CHƯA ĐO ĐƯỢC (U11), ĐANG CHẤM BẰNG AI |
| L-GIST, R-INF, S-ARG, W-CORR (20 Topics) | R-INF alone | Always paired with full Vietnamese title: R-INF · Suy luận hàm ý & Logic đoạn văn |

### **5.2 Tone, Voice, and Signage Copy Constraints (§7.5)**

Five copy invariants govern all static templates and AI diagnostic commentary (§7.5)1. Under **Rule COPY-02 (No Praise — Signboard, Not Coach)**, the interface never praises, flatters, or consoles the learner; phrases such as "Chúc mừng\!", "Tuyệt vời\!", "Bạn làm tốt lắm\!", "Đừng nản lòng\!", "Cố lên nhé\!", "Great job\!", or "Congratulations\!" are prohibited across all UI templates and blocked via system prompt rules in ai\_insight1. Under **Rule COPY-03 (No Promises)**, the interface never guarantees future test outcomes; phrasing such as "Bạn sẽ đạt B2 sau 3 tháng" is forbidden, and all trajectory statements must express conditional mathematical relationships derived from FeasibilityCalculator (such as "Với khoảng cách \~315 giờ học có hướng dẫn và quỹ thời gian 2.75 giờ/tuần, lịch học hiện tại đủ thời lượng để hoàn thành chương trình mục tiêu B2 trước ngày 15/03/2027.")1. Under **Rule COPY-04 (Every State Says What Happened and What To Do Next)**, every empty state, error banner, repeat badge (U20), re-plan notice (FR-REPLAN-03), and readiness verdict (FR-END-02) must state two factual components—what occurred in the system or measurement, and what concrete action the learner can take next—and never instruct the learner on how to feel about it1. Under **Rule COPY-05 (Every Number Carries Its Unit and Meaning)**, every numeral on screen must be set in font-mono (§4) and accompanied immediately by its unit and domain meaning (BẬC B2 · VỊ TRÍ 71/100 TRONG BẬC, ĐÚNG 14/20 CÂU (70%), CÒN \~315 GIỜ HỌC CÓ HƯỚNG DẪN, ĐÃ VIẾT: 184 / 150–220 TỪ), treating any bare unitless numeral as a defect1. Finally, under **Rule COPY-06 (No Emoji, No Raw Glyphs)**, Unicode emoji (🎉, ⚠️, 🔒, 🔥) and standalone ASCII placeholders (—, ?, \!) are prohibited; only the drawn 16×16px SVG icon set may be used, and every icon must sit beside an explicit word1.

## **6\. Deliberate Information Suppression (What Is Not Shown and Why)**

A core architectural principle of this specification is that **the user interface deliberately says less than the backend system knows** whenever exposing an internal parameter would corrupt psychometric validity, induce test anxiety, or imply false precision1. The table below specifies the seven data structures stored in the Placement and Path databases that are intentionally suppressed from learner-facing screens1.

(Revealed on SCR-PRAC-04 *only after* the answer is locked). | Showing \[B2\] or \[C1\] while answering invites the learner to skip or guess on high-level items, which corrupts measurement (U18): a candidate who avoids B2 items is misclassified as A21. |

### **7.2 Desktop-First (1440×900) Trade-Offs: What Would Break on Mobile Viewports (§8)**

Per Section 4 and Section 8 of the brief, the application is designed strictly for a desktop-first 1440×900 viewport, and no mobile layout is designed here1. If a learner accesses the application on a narrow mobile viewport (375×667px to 430×932px), five specific structural mechanisms in this specification will break and require dedicated architectural redesign in a future mobile milestone1. First, the **Two-Column Split-Pane Reading and Writing Sittings (SCR-PL-02/03, SCR-PRAC-04/05, SCR-EX-02)** rely on a 1440×900 canvas so that a 600-word C1 reading passage (55% width) and its four comprehension items plus the 200-question answer grid (45% width) share one screen with zero vertical page scrolling (§4)1. Below 960px, side-by-side columns compress below 45 characters per line, whereas stacking the passage above the questions forces vertical ping-pong scrolling that degrades reading speed and invalidates the 15.0-minute Reading placement pacing arithmetic (2.md §5.1)1. Second, **Simultaneous Multi-Item Listening Rendering (FR-SERVE-02)** requires \~780px of vertical height to display a non-scrubbable audio player alongside 3–4 simultaneous 4-option MCQ items during the 15-second pre-audio reading window; on a 667px-high mobile viewport, items 3 and 4 clip below the fold during linear audio playback2. Third, the **4-Column Per-Skill Standing Matrix (SCR-DB-01 Block 3\) and 6-Band Horizon Track (SCR-PL-04)** require a minimum horizontal container of 1180px to align four 290px skill cards or plot a 6-segment horizontal CEFR track (Pre-A1..C2) beside a 35% metadata column without truncating monospace labels1. Fourth, the **120-Cell Free Drilling Topic Matrix (SCR-PRAC-01)** relies on desktop tabular density to show topic titles, mastery badges, and local rest timestamps ("nghỉ tới 09:00 mai") in one scannable view1. Fifth, on mobile browsers, invoking the **On-Screen Virtual Keyboard during Writing Sittings (SCR-PL-03, SCR-PRAC-05)** consumes 45% of vertical viewport height, obscuring the prompt checklist and word-count bounds while typing a 220-word essay2.

### **7.3 Future v2 Accessibility Requirements and Architectural Hooks (§8)**

Although sensory and neurodivergent accessibility accommodations are out of scope for v1 by owner decision (§8), the v1 frontend state models and component props must incorporate four non-breaking architectural hooks so v2 accessibility support will not require rewriting the UI1. First, to support **Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Candidates in 4-Skill Certificates (exempt\_accommodated)**, as noted in Section 7.1 of the Placement SRS and OQ-06 of the Path SRS, a deaf learner preparing for IELTS, TOEIC\_LR, or VSTEP cannot complete acoustic Listening tasks without construct modification1. In v1, the UI's ExaminedSkillsProvider reads a dynamic array active\_modalities\[\] per path rather than hardcoding 4 cards by certificate name, and PlacementSkillResults.skill\_status reserves the enum value exempt\_accommodated2. In v2, enabling the hearing-exemption flag in /profile will set Listening to exempt\_accommodated, rendering a neutral ink-bordered badge \[MIỄN TRỪ THEO HỒ SƠ HỖ TRỢ TIẾP CẬN — KHÔNG TÍNH VÀO MỨC TỔNG QUÁT\] on SCR-PL-04, adapting SCR-DB-01 Block 3 to a 3-column grid, and unlocking synchronized transcripts during remedial steps2. Second, the **Speech-Impaired Accommodation Hook** similarly reserves exempt\_accommodated for Speaking on 4-skill certificates so overall\_cefr and the Weakest-Skill Priority Allocator compute strictly over {Listening, Reading, Writing}2. Third, the **Extended-Time and Dyslexia Rubric Hook (accommodation\_profile)** reserves a timer\_multiplier: 1.0 \| 1.5 \| 2.0 prop on the 60s Speaking recording bar (D19) and mock-exam clocks, alongside an orthographic\_exemption flag on SCR-PRAC-05 that decouples spelling errors from morphosyntactic range (W\_GR) and lexical precision (W\_LR) gates (2.md §7.1)2. Fourth, because "Bảng hiệu phòng thi" already enforces AAA contrast (\#14181d on \#ffffff), zero blur, explicit text beside every icon (§4), and zero colour-only signals, attaching aria-live="polite" attributes to the progressive grading rows on SCR-PL-04 (D5) and the \[DONE\] event (U9) of the streamed AI insight panel on SCR-PRAC-05 will make dynamic updates screen-reader accessible in v2 without altering a single visual pixel1.

## **8\. Empirical Foundations in Score Reporting, Progress Visualization, and Measurement Communication**

Every structural decision in this interface specification—particularly the design of the multi-dimensional Placement Result Screen (SCR-PL-04), the mitigation of the cross-band reset illusion (B2 · 78 ![][image3] C1 · 12), the separation of operational weekly progress from psychometric band distance (SCR-DB-01, SCR-LP-01), and the communication of measurement uncertainty (U11, D7, U12)—is grounded in peer-reviewed educational measurement, score reporting, and cognitive visualization literature1.

### **8.1 Multidimensional Score Reporting and Profile Interpretation**

Research on educational score reporting established by Hambleton and Slater (1997), Wainer, Hambleton, and Meara (1999), and Hambleton and Zenisky (2013) demonstrates that lay test takers and educators frequently misinterpret multidimensional subscores when those scores are presented as isolated numbers or aggregated into a compensatory mean4. In *Educational Measurement* and the NCME score reporting monographs, Hambleton and Zenisky (2013) emphasize that *"clear and useful score reports support users in making appropriate score inferences and have an important role to play as part of efforts to explain the validity argument for a test"* (Standard 3.1 and Cluster 5 of the AERA/APA/NCME *Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing*)4. Wainer et al. (1999, p. 304\) formulate the primary design imperative of score displays: *"Know the communicative purpose of the display and do not try to do too much"*4.  
Furthermore, Sinharay, Puhan, Haberman, and Hambleton (2019) (*Subscores: When to Communicate Them, What Are Their Alternatives, and Some Recommendations*, in Zapata-Rivera, Ed., *Score Reporting: Research and Applications*) and Yao (2010, 2012\) show that diagnostic subscores add value over a composite score only when the dimensions exhibit distinct construct profiles (such as receptive vs. productive language modalities) and when the visual display prevents false compensatory inferences5. In second-language proficiency assessment, the Council of Europe (2020) (*CEFR Companion Volume*) explicitly advocates **plurilingual and uneven profile reporting** over single-number averaging because communicative readiness in real-world academic or workplace settings is often bounded by a candidate's weakest modality2. By tethering the Overall CEFR placard on SCR-PL-04 directly to the limiting\_skill row via a Sign Gold structural bar and plotting all examined skills along a single aligned horizontal ordinate (Hambleton, 2002; Hegarty, 2019), the interface prevents compensatory averaging while making profile asymmetry immediately legible1.

### **8.2 Scale Anchoring, Vertical Articulation, and Preventing Cross-Band Reset Misinterpretation**

A well-documented cognitive pitfall in criterion-referenced growth reporting (Zenisky, Keller, & Park, 2019, *Reporting Student Growth: Challenges and Opportunities*; Kannan, Zapata-Rivera, & Bryant, 2021\) occurs when a continuous proficiency continuum (![][image84]) is partitioned into discrete performance levels (A1..C2) while also reporting a within-level location metric (0–100 intra-band position ![][image14])5. Cognitive visualization research by Hegarty (2019) (*Advances in Cognitive Science and Information Visualization*) and Cleveland and McGill (1984) demonstrates that human visual perception decodes **spatial position along a common aligned scale** far more accurately than isolated numerical labels or unaligned local bars5. When a candidate's progress is plotted on an isolated within-band bar (0–100), crossing a cut score from the top of B2 (78/100) to the bottom of C1 (12/100) creates a salient spatial contraction (78 ![][image3] 12\) that overrides the categorical label change (B2 ![][image3] C1), causing the learner to perceive growth as regression1. Replacing isolated 0–100 bars with the **Six-Segment Stepped Horizon Track** (Pre-A1..C2, where each band is a contiguous segment along a global axis ![][image69]) and prohibiting the % sign on band\_position ensures that any increase in ![][image84] always maps to a monotonic rightward spatial extension1.

### **8.3 Communicating Measurement Error, Missingness, and Dual-Axis Self-Regulated Progress**

Empirical studies by Zapata-Rivera, Kannan, and Zwick (2018, 2021\) (*Communicating Measurement Error Information to Teachers and Parents*) and Miller and Watkins (2010) reveal that test users struggle to interpret technical psychometric error terms (such as Standard Error of Measurement ![][image85] or ![][image86]\-coefficients), often confusing low measurement precision or missing data with low examinee ability5. Zapata-Rivera et al. (2018) demonstrate that pairing plain-language confidence qualifiers with visual boundary distinctions significantly reduces misinterpretation5. This finding directly anchors three rules in this SRS: rendering an unmeasured skill (skill\_status \= 'not\_measured') in a Sign Gold \#f2b705 attention frame with the explicit label CHƯA ĐO ĐƯỢC and a retry action rather than a zero/low band or a greyed-out disabled panel (U11)1; translating the single-task Generalizability Theory drop (![][image35] vs. ![][image33], Brennan, 2001\) into the explicit badge \[ƯỚC TÍNH TỪ 1/2 BÀI · ĐỘ TIN CẬY THẤP HƠN\] (D7)2; and attaching the provenance tag \[ĐIỂM DO AI ƯỚC TÍNH\] (U12) to all LLM-scored productive outputs1.  
Finally, research on formative assessment dashboards by Brown, O'Leary, and Hattie (2019) (*Effective Reporting for Formative Assessment: The asTTle Case Example*), Corrin (2019) (*Evaluating Students' Interpretation of Feedback in Interactive Dashboards*), and Locke and Latham (2002) (*Goal Setting Theory*) establishes that learners require both **proximal task feedback** (short-term controllable effort, represented by Axis 1: 04/06 weekly steps completed) and **distal mastery feedback** (distance to the criterion standard, represented by Axis 2: per-skill CEFR position and cumulative Guided Learning Hours from Cambridge Assessment English / ALTE benchmarks)3. Encoding proximal weekly steps as discrete check-boxes in Block 1 and distal band standing as continuous horizon tracks in Block 3 prevents the cognitive interference that occurs when effort and proficiency are conflated into competing percentage bars1.

Where to next?"* by separating proximal task completion from distal criterion distance5. | Grounds the Dual-Progress architecture (FR-PROG-01..03) on SCR-DB-01 and SCR-LP-01: discrete step squares for weekly work (Block 1), guided-hour ledger for feasibility (Block 2), and CEFR horizon tracks for skill distance (Block 3\)1. |
